justification: The two designs share a structure. A's sans Arabic face renders the per-mille signs correctly, while B shows tofu boxes for them on B6. A's text is also slightly more even. B's serif and lighter header and footer are pleasant, but the missing glyphs are a visible defect. Both show the same broken image-markdown text, on A3 and B3.

A uses a cleaner Arabic text face with numbered section headings and includes a table of contents (A2), which aids navigation. B replaces the headings with heavy full-width navy bands (B2, B3, B5) that dominate the pages. B's heading levels are also inconsistent, since the 'الملوحة' subhead stays plain (B6). B's body face looks more cramped and shows some missing-glyph boxes (B3). A's pages read more evenly (A3–A7).

B uses a larger body size with more generous leading, and its section heads are set in strong green bands. Running headers on every page help navigation. A sets small text across wide measures, and its plain rule-plus-heading sections are weaker. A does keep section starts cleaner, while B splits the previous section's tail onto the top of the new-section page (B3). B also shows broken diacritics from the font. Overall, B reads more comfortably and is better structured.

Design B adds a table of contents (B2), numbered section headings, and running header and footer bands with section names, which make the document easier to navigate. Its pages are filled evenly. Design A leaves large gaps, such as half-empty pages at A5 and A7. A's body text switches between sizes awkwardly; on A2, A3 and A6 the larger lead paragraphs look inconsistent. A's divider rules give it slightly stronger section breaks, but B's structure and consistent rhythm are better overall.

A uses navy band headings for clearer section markers (A3, A5), but leaves a large empty half page on A4 and an almost empty A6. B's serif body text reads more comfortably. Its text flows continuously, filling B4 and B5, and the figure sits with its section on B5. Both have the same broken image markdown on page 6 and equal imagery.

Both share identical content and flaws: the same broken markdown image text on the near-empty last page and the same missing equations. B's serif text face reads more comfortably, and its margins and line spacing are calmer. Its rule-based headings stay quietly elegant. A's heavy navy header and footer bands and its filled heading boxes give stronger section signposting, but they feel heavier, and its dense sans body is tighter.

B runs the text continuously, opens sections with clear green heading bands, carries running headers, and includes the manuscript image with a caption. A has a stylish Arabic display face, but it wastes a mostly empty page on the A3 tail and a nearly blank divider on A4, and it omits the image entirely. A's justified lines also show wide gaps. B's denser, steadier pages read better overall.

B uses full-width green section bands that make the section breaks clear, adds running headers, and sets body text in a cleaner, more consistent Arabic face. A changes type size from one paragraph to the next, with oversized lead paragraphs on A2 and A5, and its line-ruled section breaks are weaker. B does show missing-glyph boxes for the per-mille signs on B6. A's typography is still less even overall.

A uses full-width green section bands with clear white headings and generous line spacing. Running heads and footers frame each page consistently. B's section headings are small, set under thin rules, and weak. B also oddly enlarges the lead paragraphs, and its text is denser with tighter leading. Its page 6 leaves a large empty area. A's per-mille glyphs render as boxes, but overall A reads more cleanly.

B uses a cleaner, consistent sans Arabic face with even paragraph sizing. Its strong navy section bands and running header/footer bars give clear structure. A's thin rules and plain headings feel weaker. A also has inconsistent lead-paragraph sizes, with larger first paragraphs, which disrupt rhythm.

Design A sets the Arabic body in a larger, more legible Naskh face with generous leading, and marks its sections with strong green heading bands and running headers. Design B uses a smaller, cramped Arabic font that renders some characters as missing-glyph boxes (B2). Its section heads hang under thin rules with weak presence, and the body size is inconsistent: the first paragraph on B4 is larger than the rest. A's text pages read more comfortably, though its section breaks leave some top-heavy gaps.

A pairs a serif body with sans headings and uses numbered headings, which gives a clearer hierarchy. Its section-opener page (A3) is mostly empty, and the intro page (A2) is half blank. B's light-weight H1 headings (B2, B4) are weaker than its bold H2s, which inverts the hierarchy. B also strands the map alone on its last page with no text (B6). A keeps that map with its text (A7). Overall A reads more polished.

A sets the text in a more comfortable Naskh-style face with generous line spacing and keeps paragraphs well spaced. Its pages end at natural breaks, and the per-mille glyphs fail in only a few spots on A6. B uses a geometric sans that is denser and harder to read in Arabic. B also crams text, runs paragraphs across page breaks (B4, B5), and leaves an awkwardly empty bottom on B6. Its heavy header and footer bars add clutter. Both use similar section bands and the same image.

A has a table of contents, numbered section headings in a bold, clear weight, and consistent header and footer bands with running heads. Its text column is comfortable. B has no TOC. Its headings are small and unnumbered and get lost against the body text. B's body text is smaller and denser with wider lines, and it shows missing-glyph boxes on page 2. B is uneven too: section headings with large top gaps, and an orphaned subsection on B6.

A includes a table of contents (A2) and numbered section headings. Its running header and footer bands frame each page consistently (A3–A7). Body text is set at a steady size throughout. B has no TOC, and its headings are unnumbered and weaker. B also swells the lead paragraph after each heading to a larger size (B3, B6), which makes the text rhythm uneven. Its thin top rule and plain footer give less structure than A's.

A uses a consistent Naskh-style body font with clear full-width green section bands and running headers, which gives strong section hierarchy. B's geometric Kufi-like font is less comfortable for long Arabic text. B also inconsistently enlarges the opening paragraphs after headings (B2, B3, B6), so its rhythm is uneven. A renders the per-mille symbols as missing-glyph boxes (A6), a minor flaw.

A keeps a consistent sans-serif voice and a uniform text column under clear navy header and footer bands. Its section heads are styled consistently. B mixes things up in several ways. The H2 headings hang outdented past the text column (B2, B5). The Characteristics intro paragraph is set oversized (B2). B4 leaves a large empty area under the diagram, and B5 opens with a gap at the top. A has its own weak spots: a light H2 weight (A2, A4) and a mostly empty final page carrying only the map (A6). Even so, it reads more coherently overall.

B adds a table of contents (B2), numbered section headings that stand out clearly (B4, B5, B7), and consistent header and footer bands. Its text is larger and more readable, though the lines are a little tight. A's headings are weak and small, especially on A6, and it has no TOC. A wastes space with near-empty page breaks before each section (A3, A4), but its body text is denser. Both show the same broken image markdown (A3, B5).

A uses consistent header/footer bands and solid section heading bars that clearly mark sections, and places the map image with its section heading on A5. B has a strong serif text face but awkward hanging-indent body text with outdented headings, a half-empty page B5 after the image, and a section starting low on B6. A wastes nearly all of A6 on a broken image link, but B shows the same artifact, so overall A reads more cleanly and consistently.

B adds a table of contents, running header and footer bands with section names, and includes the manuscript image with a caption on B8. A's text reads cleanly in its Arabic face, but it leaves a mostly empty page (A3) and has an awkward divider page (A4). It also omits the image, and its 'إسهاماته' heading on A6 sits on a page that breaks oddly. Both show the leftover raw image-path text.

A renders all glyphs cleanly, including the Greek and per-mille signs, and adds a table of contents. B shows missing-glyph boxes (B3, B6) and drops section numbers. B's green section bands are visually strong, but they break the page flow and do not outweigh A's cleaner, more complete text rendering (A3, A7).

A sets the body in a larger, more open Arabic sans with generous leading, so the long paragraphs read comfortably. Its section headings stand out clearly. B packs smaller text with longer lines, so the pages feel dense and grey and are harder to read. Its smaller headings also give a weaker hierarchy. B's running headers that echo section names are a nice touch, but the cost to readability outweighs this. The covers and the image treatment are similar in both.

Both designs share the same broken equations and the raw markdown image link on the last page. A sets its body in a serif face, which reads more comfortably than B's narrow sans. A also numbers its headings (A3, A5). B's heading bands are stronger section markers (B3, B5). B places the map at the top of a page so it opens a clean section (B5). B4 ends cleanly at a paragraph break. A's figure sits mid-flow after a paragraph spilling over from the previous page (A5). Overall B has the better page structure, by a narrow margin.

A uses a consistent sans Arabic face with comfortable leading and strong navy section bands with clear headers and footers, giving a clear hierarchy. B's section heads are small bold text under thin rules, and its body sizes vary oddly: lead paragraphs are larger and later paragraphs denser and smaller on B5, which feels inconsistent. B's text is also tighter. A has some justification gaps on A3, but overall it reads more cleanly.

A uses a readable Arabic serif face, clear green heading bands that tie in with the cover, and includes the manuscript image with its caption (A7). B has an odd chapter divider that is mostly empty (B4), a short-filled page (B3), and its display-style font is less comfortable for long reading. B also drops the image entirely, and its second chapter has no divider despite the TOC promising one (B6).

B includes the manuscript image with a caption (B7), which A lacks. That outweighs A's strengths. A's larger, more open Arabic text with generous leading reads more comfortably (A2, A6). A also has a section divider page (A4). B's body text is smaller with a long, dense measure (B2, B5), and section headings sit mid-flow. Still, B's figure gives the document substance and keeps it more complete.

B's section divider (B3) cuts the Characteristics intro off from its bullet list, leaving a mostly empty page and splitting the list content onto B4. B2 is also half-empty, and the B3 divider sidebar band looks heavy. B has stronger numbered headings, but its flow is broken. A runs continuously, keeps the lists intact, and places its figures closer to their text. A6 still leaves an orphaned map page, as B7 also does.

Design B pairs a clean Arabic sans with a table of contents (B2) and numbered headings. It also renders the per-mille signs correctly, where Design A shows tofu boxes (A6 vs B7). Design A's full-width green section bands are striking but break the flow. B's dark header and footer bars are heavier, but its text reads more consistently.

B uses solid navy section bands with running headers and footers. These give the document clear structure and a consistent page frame, and the text fills the pages evenly. A's sections are marked only by thin rules. A also mixes a larger lead-paragraph size inconsistently (A2, A3, A6), and A5 and A7 end half-empty. B's pages are denser but steadier in rhythm.

A uses bold sans headings with outdented placement, giving clearer section hierarchy than B's light serif headings. B's dense body text runs wide, and B6 is an almost-empty page holding only a stray image-markdown line. A has large gaps after the image on A5 and at the top of A6, and A also shows the broken markdown on A6, but its pages are better distributed overall.

B sets the Arabic in a cleaner, more uniform sans with steady line spacing and margins. A uses a Naskh face whose Latin glyphs look odd and whose lines are tight and dense (A4, A5). B adds a consistent top rule band that frames each page and its sections breathe more (B3, B6). A's cover and running heads are fine but its pages feel cramped.

B uses full-width green section bands with running heads that clearly mark sections, and it packs text more evenly. A's lead-paragraph enlargements create inconsistent text sizes (A3, A6), and its large gaps leave pages unevenly filled (A5, A7). B has tofu glyphs for the per-mille sign (B6), a minor flaw. A's pages look somewhat airier, but its rhythm is uneven.

The two designs share the same content and the same flaws: broken equations and a raw image markdown string on the last page. A sets the text in a serif with comfortable leading and keeps the chrome to a thin top rule and a quiet footer, so it reads as a calmer, book-like document. B adds heavy navy header and footer bars on every page plus filled heading bands. These give stronger section cues but add visual weight. B's tighter, denser sans text body is also somewhat harder to read over long runs.

A keeps the manuscript image (A7), while B drops it. A sets body text in a more compact Naskh-style face that reads comfortably. B's geometric Arabic face is large and less refined, and its intro spills onto a mostly empty B3. B also inserts a near-empty divider page (B4) that announces two sections, and its first section heading is easy to miss. A's flow is steadier, though A6 and A7 leave notable empty space.

A provides a table of contents, consistent navy header/footer bands, and a cleaner sans text face with generous spacing. B has strong green section bands that give clear chapter breaks, but its cover rule is nearly invisible, it lacks a TOC, and it leaves a raw broken image-markdown string after body text on B3, while A isolates it at the top of A5. A's dense body pages are slightly more even and readable.

B adds a table of contents and numbered section headings, and its header and footer bands make navigation clear. Its sans Arabic face is uniform in size. A uses inconsistent sizes: lead paragraphs are set larger than the body (A2, A3, A5). Its section headings are weaker, and a rule separates each section. B's justified text flows evenly (B3–B7). A's Naskh face is somewhat more elegant, and its image placement on A5 is cleaner. Still, B's structure and consistency win.

A uses a refined serif with comfortable leading and headings aligned to the text column, which reads calmly. B's spaced sans/serif mix and its outdented headings look less cohesive, and B5 leaves a large empty gap below the map. A's map sits well with the following section. Both show the raw image-markdown leak, but A strands it on an otherwise empty page (A6), which is a notable flaw. B's running section headers are a plus. On balance A's typography and pacing are stronger.

Design A's full-width navy heading bands are bold and give strong section breaks. But A justifies its text with wide inter-word gaps, and the large bands interrupt the flow (A2, A3, A5). Design B adds a table of contents (B2) and uses numbered plain headings with a cleaner Arabic face. Its paragraph setting reads more evenly, giving calmer, more consistent pages (B3–B7).

A has a coherent banded header/footer system and a striking section divider page, but that divider (A3) holds only two lines of intro text and leaves a huge empty area, and A2 is half empty. B flows more continuously with fewer half-empty pages (B2, B3, B5), giving a steadier reading rhythm. B's hanging section heads with rules give clear hierarchy. B4 still has a large gap below the figure, and A's numbered sections are a plus, but B reads more efficiently overall.

Both designs carry the same raw markdown image link on page 6, which reads as a defect in each. A uses an elegant serif with thin rule headers and lighter running elements. Its pages break cleanly at section starts, and the map sits at the top of A5 with its section heading directly below. B uses heavy dark header and footer bands on every page. Its text flows across pages, with a split word at the B2–B3 break, and its dense serif body justifies into wider gaps. B's numbered sans headings do aid navigation, but overall A looks calmer and more refined.

A uses a lighter, more refined serif with hanging section headings set off by rules (A3, A6), which gives clearer hierarchy. It also leaves the page edges uncluttered. B frames every page with heavy dark header and footer bands (B2–B6) that compete with the text, and its body text is denser and narrower. A has more empty space after the figure on A5, and both end with a stray markdown line (A6, B6). On balance, A reads more calmly.

Both share the same content flaws (empty equations, raw markdown image link). A flows continuously, with the map followed by the next section on A5. B leaves large voids: half of B5 is empty below the map, and B6 starts low on the page. B's headings hang outdented past the text column, and its letterspaced body text on B5 looks uneven. A's header and footer bands are heavy but consistent. Overall A reads more evenly.

B's chapter divider page (B3) strands a single intro sentence ending in a colon, separating it from its bullet list on the next page, and B2 leaves the bottom half of the page empty. A flows continuously, keeping the Characteristics intro with its list on A2. A's headings sit in the left margin with indented body text, which reads cleanly. B's running header and footer bands and numbered sections add some navigation, but the broken flow and wasted space outweigh them. Both designs leave the lower half of the map page blank.

A provides a table of contents, consistent running headers and footers, and numbered section headings. It also includes the manuscript image with a caption on its final page. B omits the image entirely. B also spends a whole page on a chapter-divider spread (B4), and B3 is left largely empty. B's 'الجبر' subheading is weak, and its Arabic display face is less readable at body size. A's pacing is steadier, although its section heading falls mid-page.

A uses heavier dark header/footer bands with running section titles and page numbers, and bold numbered headings that stand out clearly. B's light Garamond-style text is denser and paler, and its thin-ruled headings are weaker. Both share the broken equations and the stray Z-scheme markdown on page 6. B's lead-in paragraph under Overview is also oddly enlarged.

A pairs a serif text face with bold sans headings, giving clear section hierarchy, and keeps the world map with its text on A6. Its quiet footers frame the pages lightly. A's weak spots are the large blank areas on A4 and A6 and the half-empty top of A5. B's light-weight H1 headings ("Characteristics", "Tidal constituents") are weaker than its H2s, which inverts the hierarchy. B's heavy dark header and footer bands crowd every page, and B6 strands the map alone on a mostly blank page.

B adds a table of contents and numbered headings, which give clearer navigation and hierarchy. Its consistent header and footer bands frame each page, and its sections run on without forced breaks. A's full-width green section bands are strong, but they leave awkward partial pages (A3 starts with a two-line orphan). A's serif Arabic face reads slightly more elegantly. Both designs leak a broken image path (A3, B5).

A applies a consistent text size and strong navy heading bands with running headers, which gives clear, steady section markers. B enlarges the first paragraph after each heading (B2, B3, B6), so body text jumps in size. B3 ends with a lot of empty space, and B5 leaves a large blank area at the bottom. A's pages are denser but more uniform (A2–A6).

A has a table of contents, numbered section headings, and consistent header and footer bands. Its Arabic sans body text is uniform and clear. B's body text is small and dense, and its type size is inconsistent: on B5 the first paragraph is larger than the second. B's headings are weak, set small beside rules, and some glyphs render as boxes on B3. A's leading and paragraph rhythm read more evenly.

A sets the body in a warm serif with comfortable leading and outdented rule-topped headings. Its weaknesses are a large empty area below the map on A5 and a section start pushed down on A6. B's heavy navy header and footer bands and solid heading bars are strong, but its condensed sans body is denser. B4 ends half-empty, and B6 is a near-blank page holding only a stray markdown line. Both carry that broken image reference, but B isolates it on its own page, which looks worse.
